subject.title: Regression: exec intermittently unavailable in isolated cron sessions (was fixed in 2026.4.1)

question: Should cron `toolsAllow` be treated as operator intent that can override restrictive profile/provider caps for shell tools, and should unavailable required tools fail pre-dispatch with structured metadata rather than assistant-summary text?
rationale: The remaining fixes change scheduled command-execution exposure and failure classification semantics, so automation should not choose that security/product boundary from issue text alone.

options.title: Adopt structured fail-closed semantics
options.body: Require unavailable required tools to fail before dispatch or via structured runtime metadata, and approve only scoped shell exposure where maintainers accept the security boundary.

options.title: Accept wildcard cron override only
options.body: Land the narrow wildcard/profile PR while keeping finite allowlists and provider-specific tool gaps tracked separately.

options.title: Pause for broader cron tool policy
options.body: Keep linked PRs paused until maintainers decide one permanent cron tool-surface contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt structured fail-closed semantics
recommendation.body: Require unavailable required tools to fail before dispatch or via structured runtime metadata, and approve only scoped shell exposure where maintainers accept the security boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent GitHub path history shows broad work across cron run/session handling, Codex dynamic tools, and cron status helpers relevant to this policy choice.
